Case study · Heritage / Extension

Harbour Extension: adding 38 m² to a heritage villa with zero revisions

Gain heritage and planning consent for meaningful additional living space, without modifying the protected fabric of the original building.

Client
Private client
Year
2025
Timeline
Pre-application 4 weeks
Services
5 delivered

Results

  • 0 Drawing revisions
  • +38 m² Floor area
  • -4% vs. budget

Full case study

01

The challenge

A protected 1930s villa with a rear garden the family barely used. Heritage rules forbade altering the listed rear elevation, which ruled out the obvious extension. Two architects had already proposed touching the original brick and been refused at pre-application.

02

The goal

Gain heritage and planning consent for meaningful additional living space, without modifying the protected fabric of the original building.

03

Approach

  1. 01 Walked the site and identified that the constraint was also the opportunity: the untouched brick could become an interior surface.
  2. 02 Set the new volume eleven metres from the original, connected by a fully glazed link, so no protected fabric was touched.
  3. 03 Specified the link in blackened steel and glass to read clearly as a later addition — the approach conservation officers prefer.
  4. 04 Ran pre-application meetings early with drawings that explained the heritage reasoning, not just the design.
  5. 05 Detailed the threshold at 1:5 so the junction between old brick and new structure was resolved before tender.
04

Services provided

  • Feasibility
  • Heritage pre-application
  • Concept design
  • Detailed design
  • Site supervision
05

Results

Consent was granted with no drawing revisions requested — the pre-application conversation had already answered the officer’s concerns. The completed extension added 38 m² of kitchen and dining space and finished 4% under the agreed construction budget. The original brick elevation now reads as a feature wall from inside the new link.
